newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields drop again as U.S. soothed.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields drop again as U.S. soothed.

text.p: *Australian bond yields dropped smartly in early trading as a string of market-friendly U.S. data helped to soothe U.S. Treasuries and pushed out fears of a Fed rate hike to November.
Australian bond yields again dropped smartly in early trading as a string of market-friendly U.S. data helped to soothe U.S. Treasuries and pushed out fears of a Fed rate hike to November.

Local bill futures continued to strike higher with the December position setting a new contract high of 95.26 and fully discounting a 25 basis point easing in current 5.0 percent official interest rates.
Thursday's benign final wages data for the second quarter has stirred up thoughts of a further easing in monetary policy, with several economists expecting the next move in November.
The 10-year bond futures contract is now back to where it ended last week at around 93.420 having slumped to 93.135 on Wednesday and largely due to recent weakness in U.S. Treasuries.
The U.S. market closed sharply higher after a series of market-friendly data confirmed inflation was well under control.

The July CPI showed a modest 0.2 percent rise, industrial production also rose 0.2 percent for the same month, while capacity utilisation fell to 83.1 percent. The U.S. PPI earlier this week also fell for the seventh consecutive month, while retail sales grew less than feared.
There is no local data due for release on Friday.

The local market continued Thursday's outperformance against the dollar bloc, particularly against Canada, which also lagged the U.S. rally. The negative spreads to New Zealand widened once again. N.Z. June quarter retail sales were slightly stronger than expected.
